angle: Enterprises lose AI programs to trust debt, not model error—design trust into the product.
sourceTitle: Earning and sustaining trust in the age of AI
linkedinPost:
Most AI programs don’t fail on accuracy—they fail on trust.

McKinsey’s conversation with Invesco’s CEO nails it: AI has to sit inside the core strategy and customer promise. Once you burn trust, you don’t get a second try.

From the front lines, “trust-by-design” beats post-hoc explainers every time. The teams that ship responsibly do four things:

1) Show data lineage like a receipt—what data grounded this answer?
2) Offer easy escalation and human appeal, with SLAs a manager signs.
3) Log every decision with why/why-not reasoning for audit.
4) Red-team with customer ops in the room, not just engineers.

We also freeze go-lives until we can answer one question on a dashboard: “Can we explain this recommendation in one sentence a customer would believe?” If not, it’s not ready—no matter the model score.

Trust isn’t a marketing campaign; it’s part of the product spec and the controls. You ship it, or you don’t.

What’s the one trust control you’d refuse to launch without? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #CustomerExperience
